## FreshCart Restaurant Partner Agreement (extract)

Schedule 4 - Cost allocation for customer refunds

## 4.1 Allocation principle

Where a refund is issued to a customer, the cost of that refund is borne by the party responsible for the underlying failure, determined as set out in this Schedule.

## 4.2 Partner-borne events

The Partner bears the full cost of the refund where the failure arises from food preparation, incorrect items despatched, missing items at the point of handover, or packaging inadequate for transport of liquid contents.

Packaging adequacy is assessed against the FreshCart Packaging Standard current at the time of the order. Repeated packaging failures may trigger review under clause 9.

## 4.3 Platform-borne events

FreshCart bears the full cost of the refund where the failure arises from delivery partner handling, delivery delay beyond the committed window, or application error.

## 4.4 Shared events

Where responsibility cannot be determined from available evidence within the review period, the cost is shared equally between the parties.

## 4.5 Disputes

The Partner may dispute an allocation within fifteen days of the monthly statement. Disputes are resolved under clause 12.

refund_policy_v2_2022.pdf.text:
## FreshCart Customer Refund Policy

Version 2.0 · Effective 15 June 2022

## 1. Scope

This policy governs refunds for food delivery orders placed through the FreshCart consumer application. It applies to all orders in India from the effective date above.

## 2. Eligible reasons for refund

A customer is eligible to request a refund where the order was not delivered, was delivered materially incomplete, arrived in a spilled or damaged condition, or where the items delivered do not match the items ordered.

## 2.1 Spillage and damage

Spillage means leakage of contents from the packaging. All spillage claims attract a full refund of item value. Photographic evidence must be submitted within 12 hours of delivery.

## 3. Claim frequency limits

A customer may make up to two refund claims in any rolling thirty day period. A third and any subsequent claim within that period is automatically declined.

## 4. Refund timelines

Approved refunds are credited to the original payment method within seven to ten working days.

## 5. Exclusions

Refunds are not available where the customer provided an incorrect delivery address or where the claim is made more than 24 hours after the delivery timestamp.

refund_policy_v3_2024.pdf.text:
## FreshCart Customer Refund Policy

Version 3.0 · Effective 01 April 2024 · Supersedes v2.0 (2022)

## 1. Scope

This policy governs refunds for food delivery orders placed through the FreshCart consumer application. It applies to all orders in India from the effective date above. Restaurant partner liability is governed separately by the Partner Agreement.

## 2. Eligible reasons for refund

A customer is eligible to request a refund where the order was not delivered, was delivered materially incomplete, arrived in a spilled or damaged condition, or where the items delivered do not match the items ordered.

## 2.1 Spillage and damage

Spillage means leakage of liquid or semi-solid contents from the packaging such that the item is unfit for consumption. Partial leakage that does not render the item unfit is assessed as damage and attracts a partial refund of up to fifty percent of item value. Photographic evidence must be submitted within 24 hours of delivery.

## 3. Claim frequency limits

A customer may make up to three refund claims in any rolling thirty day period. A fourth and any subsequent claim within that period is automatically declined by the system and must be escalated to a support supervisor for manual review. This limit was raised from two claims under v2.0 of this policy.

## 4. Refund timelines

Approved refunds are credited to the original payment method within five to seven working days. Wallet credit, where the customer elects it, is applied immediately.

## 5. Exclusions

Refunds are not available where the customer provided an incorrect delivery address, where delivery was refused without cause, or where the claim is made more than 48 hours after the delivery timestamp.

support_escalation_sop_scanned.pdf.text:
## FreshCart Support Escalation SOP

Document SOP-SUP-014 Revision 5 March 2024

## 1. When to escalate to a supervisor

A support agent must escalate to a supervisor where the customer has exceeded the claim frequency limit set out in the Customer Refund Policy, where the order value exceeds INR 5,000, or where the customer has raised a complaint about a previous refund decision.

## 2. Evidence required before escalation

The agent must attach the order identifier, the delivery timestamp, any photographic evidence submitted by the customer, and the customer's claim history for the preceding thirty days.

## 3. Supervisor response time

Supervisors must respond to an escalated case within four working hours. Cases unresolved after eight working hours are routed automatically to the regional support manager.

support_qbr_q1_2024.pptx.text:
Support Operations QBR — Q1 2024

Prepared for the Support Leadership Review, 12 April 2024

Refund volume and rate

Refund claim volume rose 18 percent quarter on quarter. Order volume rose 22 percent over the same period, so the refund rate fell slightly from 4.4 percent to 4.2 percent.

Action: revise the spillage evidence window from 24 hours after partner feedback in Q2.

Escalation performance

P2 cases represented 61 percent of all escalations, driven mainly by spillage claims on liquid-heavy orders.

Escalations exceeding the four hour supervisor response target: 312 cases, concentrated in the Delhi NCR and Bengaluru regions during the evening peak.

## FreshCart Support SLA Matrix

Document SLA-SUP-2024-02 · Effective 01 April 2024 · Owner: Support Operations

The following turnaround times apply to customer contacts received through the in-app chat channel. TAT is measured from first customer message to first substantive agent response, excluding automated acknowledgements.

### Turnaround targets by priority

| **Priority**   | **Trigger**                                          | **First response TAT**   | **Resolution TAT**   | **Escalation path**    |
|----------------|------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|----------------------|------------------------|
| P1             | Order value over INR 5,000, or food safety complaint | 15 minutes               | 2 hours              | Supervisor immediately |
| P2             | Non-delivery, or spillage with photographic evidence | 30 minutes               | 4 hours              | Supervisor at 3 hours  |
| P3             | Partial order issue, or incorrect item               | 2 hours                  | 24 hours             | Supervisor at 18 hours |
| P4             | General query, account or wallet question            | 4 hours                  | 48 hours             | None                   |

### Notes

TAT targets are suspended during declared platform incidents.

Claim frequency checks are performed before a P2 case is accepted; see the Customer Refund Policy for the applicable limit.
